children: Caterpillar reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $20.682 billion, up 17% from a year earlier, while net income attributable to common shareholders rose 43% to $3.287 billion and diluted EPS increased 46% to $7.13. Growth was supported by higher sales volume and favorable price realization.
Revenue was $20.682B, compared with $17.638B in the prior-year quarter; YoY change 17%.
Net income attributable to common shareholders was $3.287B, compared with $2.300B; YoY change 43%.
Diluted EPS was $7.13, compared with $4.88; YoY change 46%.
Power & Energy revenue grew 18%, Construction Industries revenue rose 18%, and Resource Industries revenue increased 15%. Data-center power demand supported Power & Energy.
Dealer inventories increased $800M during the quarter. Management cited strong end-user equipment demand, order rates and a growing backlog.
Caterpillar expects full-year 2026 revenue growth in the mid-to-high teens, with strong end-user sales and services growth across its primary segments.
Capacity expansions remain on schedule. Caterpillar completed its acquisition of Fabick on October 31, 2026.
